questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related with Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Article 368**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ • **Article 368** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the **power of Parliament to amend the Constitution** and the procedure for such amendments. • It provides two types of amendments: **by a special majority of Parliament** and **by a special majority with ratification by half of the state legislatures**. • The article specifies that an amendment to the Constitution does not constitute a law under Article 13, meaning it cannot be invalidated on the grounds of violating fundamental rights. • **Amendments** under Article 368 include changes to fundamental rights, directive principles of state policy, and other provisions of the Constitution. • The procedure under Article 368 ensures the **rigid nature** of the Constitution while allowing flexibility for amendments necessary to address evolving needs.

questions.question: The New Development Bank is associated with which of the following international organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BRICS**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **New Development Bank (NDB)** is an international financial institution established by the member countries of **BRICS**, which includes **Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**.

• The bank was founded in **July 2014** during the 6th BRICS Summit held in **Fortaleza, Brazil**, and became operational in **2015**.

• The primary purpose of the NDB is to **mobilize resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects** in emerging economies and developing countries.

• The bank aims to complement the existing efforts of multilateral and regional financial institutions, such as the World Bank and IMF, in addressing development challenges.

• The headquarters of the New Development Bank is located in **Shanghai, China**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Key Features of BRICS:**

• **BRICS** is an acronym for the grouping of the world's major emerging economies: **Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**.

• It was originally known as **BRIC** before the inclusion of **South Africa** in 2010.

• The group represents about **42% of the world's population**, **23% of global GDP**, and **16% of world trade**.

• **Functions of the New Development Bank:**

• The NDB provides financial assistance for **infrastructure development** and **sustainable development projects** in BRICS and other emerging economies.

• It offers financial products like **loans, equity participation, guarantees, and technical assistance**.

• The bank promotes the use of local currencies in its operations to reduce dependency on major global currencies like the US Dollar.

• **Governance Structure of NDB:**

• The NDB is governed by a **Board of Governors** and a **Board of Directors** comprising representatives from the member countries.

• The first President of the NDB was **K. V. Kamath** from India.

• The presidency of the bank rotates every five years among the member countries.

• **Comparison with Other Institutions:**

• Unlike the **World Bank** and **IMF**, which have been criticized for their Western-centric governance structures, the NDB aims to give equal voting rights to all its members.

• The NDB focuses specifically on infrastructure and sustainable development in emerging economies, differentiating it from global financial institutions that have a broader scope.

questions.question: Where was the BIMSTEC Summit held in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thailand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bangkok, Thailand**, hosted the BIMSTEC Summit in **April 2025**. The summit aims to strengthen economic and technical cooperation among member nations of BIMSTEC.
 
• **BIMSTEC** stands for the **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation**, which includes seven member countries: **Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, and Thailand**.
 
• The summit focused on enhancing collaboration in areas such as **trade, investment, connectivity, energy, and climate change**, reflecting the strategic importance of the Bay of Bengal region.
 
• Thailand, being one of the founding members of BIMSTEC, plays a crucial role in fostering regional cooperation and hosted this summit to discuss pressing issues and strengthen regional ties.
 
• The 2025 summit emphasized the need for **regional connectivity** projects, such as the BIMSTEC Master Plan for Transport Connectivity, which aims to improve infrastructural links among member states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BIMSTEC Overview:**

 
 
• **Founded:** BIMSTEC was established in **1997** through the Bangkok Declaration.
 
• **Members:** It comprises **seven countries**: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, and Thailand.
 
• **Purpose:** The organization aims to enhance collaboration in key sectors such as **trade, technology, energy, and transport connectivity**.
 
• **Geographical Importance:** The Bay of Bengal region is home to approximately **1.5 billion people**, accounting for nearly **22% of the global population**.
 
 
 
• **Key Sectors of BIMSTEC Cooperation:**
 
 
• **Trade and Investment:** Promoting free trade agreements and boosting investments among member states.
 
• **Connectivity:** Developing transport corridors and infrastructure projects to enhance regional connectivity.
 
• **Climate Change:** Addressing environmental challenges and ensuring sustainable development in the region.
 
• **Energy Cooperation:** Exploring renewable energy options and improving energy security.
 
 
 
• **Significant Achievements of BIMSTEC:**
 
 
• Completion of the **BIMSTEC Master Plan for Transport Connectivity**, aimed at integrating transport networks in the region.
 
• Successful collaboration in disaster management and humanitarian assistance.
 
• Initiatives to combat terrorism and transnational crimes within member states.
 
• Efforts to enhance cultural and people-to-people connectivity through tourism and academic exchanges.
 
 
 
• **Important Developments:**
 
 
• The BIMSTEC Secretariat was established in **Dhaka, Bangladesh** in **2014** to facilitate coordination among member states.
 
• In recent years, BIMSTEC has gained strategic importance as an alternative to other regional groupings, focusing on economic and technical cooperation.
 
• Member countries have prioritized the development of the Bay of Bengal region, aligning with their national interests and global goals.

questions.question: Amitabh Bachchan had been selected for the Dada Saheb Phalke award for the year ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2018**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amitabh Bachchan**, often referred to as the "Shahenshah of Bollywood," was selected for the prestigious **Dada Saheb Phalke Award** in the year **2018**.
 
• The **Dada Saheb Phalke Award** is considered India's highest award in the field of cinema. It is conferred by the Government of India for outstanding contribution to the growth and development of Indian cinema.
 
• Amitabh Bachchan received the award in recognition of his **immense contribution to Indian cinema** over a career spanning several decades.
 
• The award was officially announced by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting in **September 2019**, and he was honored during the **National Film Awards ceremony**.
 
• The Dada Saheb Phalke Award includes a **Swarna Kamal (Golden Lotus)**, a shawl, and a cash prize of **10 lakh rupees**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dada Saheb Phalke Award:**

 
 
• Named after **Dadasaheb Phalke**, the "Father of Indian Cinema," who directed India's first full-length feature film, **Raja Harishchandra**, in 1913.
 
• First awarded in **1969**, the inaugural recipient was **Devika Rani**, known as the "First Lady of Indian Cinema."
 
• The award is given annually at the National Film Awards ceremony by the Directorate of Film Festivals, under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
 
• Recipients are chosen based on their significant contribution to the art of cinema, spanning acting, direction, production, writing, and music, among others.
 
 
 
• **Amitabh Bachchan's Legacy:**
 
 
• Amitabh Bachchan, born on **October 11, 1942**, is one of the most influential and iconic actors in Indian cinema.
 
• He gained popularity in the 1970s with films like **Zanjeer**, **Deewar**, and **Sholay**, earning him the title "Angry Young Man."
 
• Over his career, he has acted in more than **200 films** and won numerous accolades, including **4 National Film Awards** and multiple **Filmfare Awards**.
 
• In addition to acting, he has worked as a playback singer, television host, and producer, and he remains an influential figure in Indian culture.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Recipients of the Dada Saheb Phalke Award:**
 
 
• **Raj Kapoor** (1987): Renowned actor and filmmaker known for his contributions to Indian cinema's golden era.
 
• **Lata Mangeshkar** (1989): The "Nightingale of India," famous for her unparalleled contribution to Indian music.
 
• **Yash Chopra** (2001): Legendary filmmaker known for romantic hits like **Dil To Pagal Hai** and **Veer-Zaara**.
 
• **Rajinikanth** (2019): Superstar of Tamil cinema with a massive fan following across India and overseas.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Information and Broadcasting** oversees the selection process for the Dada Saheb Phalke Award.
 
• The award honors individuals who have made a lasting impact on Indian cinema and its global recognition.
 
• It is not limited to actors and directors but also includes individuals from other film-related fields like cinematography, music, and screenwriting.
 
• The recognition serves as a testament to the recipient's lifelong dedication to the Indian film industry.
 
 

``

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian female doctor of western medicine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anandibai Gopalrao Joshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anandibai Gopalrao Joshi** was the first Indian female doctor to practice western medicine. She earned her medical degree at the age of **19**.
 
• She graduated from the **Woman's Medical College of Pennsylvania** (now part of Drexel University College of Medicine) in **1886**.
 
• Anandibai was born in **Kalyan, Maharashtra**, in **1865**. She faced significant societal opposition due to her decision to study medicine abroad.
 
• Her enrollment in medical school was largely inspired by a personal tragedy—the death of her child due to inadequate medical care, which motivated her to become a doctor.
 
• Despite her early demise at the age of **21** due to tuberculosis, Anandibai remains a pioneer who broke societal norms and paved the way for women in India to enter the medical field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **EK Janaki Ammal:**

 
 
• She was an **Indian botanist** and geneticist, known for her contributions to cytogenetics and plant breeding.
 
• She became the first Indian woman to receive a doctorate in **botany**.
 
• She contributed to the development of hybrid sugarcane varieties and worked extensively in **London** and **India**.
 
 
 
• **Rupa Bai Furdoonji:**
 
 
• She is recognized as the first female anesthesiologist in the world.
 
• She graduated from the **Madras Medical College** in the **19th century** and contributed to the field of anesthesiology.
 
• Her achievements in the field of medicine were crucial in creating awareness about anesthesiology in India.
 
 
 
• **Mary Poonen Lukose:**
 
 
• Mary Poonen Lukose was the first woman surgeon general in India.
 
• She graduated in medicine from **England** and returned to India to contribute to public health and medical services.
 
• She played a significant role in modernizing healthcare services in **Kerala**.
 
 
 
• **Anandibai Gopalrao Joshi:**
 
 
• Anandibai was among the first Indian women to earn a degree in western medicine, breaking barriers for future generations.
 
• Her journey was marked by perseverance and dedication, despite severe societal resistance.
 
• Her graduation was celebrated as a remarkable achievement, not just for herself but for Indian women as a whole.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** Anandibai's achievements were groundbreaking during the late **19th century**, a time when women's education in India was rare.
 
• **Recognition:** She received appreciation letters from Queen Victoria and other notable figures for her determination.
 
• **Legacy:** Anandibai's legacy inspires generations of women to pursue careers in medicine and other fields traditionally dominated by men.
 
• **Challenges:** Her story reflects the social barriers faced by women in India during colonial rule, highlighting the importance of education and perseverance.

questions.question: In July 2024, Om Prakash Mathur has been appointed as Governor of ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• In **July 2024**, **Om Prakash Mathur**, a senior politician and member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), was appointed as the **Governor of Sikkim**. This appointment reflects his significant contributions to Indian politics and public administration. 
• The position of a **Governor** in India is constitutionally significant and is appointed by the **President of India** under **Article 155** of the Indian Constitution. 
• **Sikkim**, a northeastern state in India, is strategically located and shares international borders with **China, Bhutan, and Nepal**. The role of the Governor in such states is crucial for maintaining administrative efficiency and security. 
• Om Prakash Mathur has had an extensive career in politics, serving in various capacities within the BJP and contributing to the development of the party, particularly in Rajasthan, his home state. 
• The appointment of Governors is often based on political and administrative experience. It is a standard practice for the central government to appoint individuals with a proven track record of service and governance. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Role of a Governor:** 
• The Governor serves as the **constitutional head** of the state, with the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers serving as the executive authority. 
• The Governor acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers but also has certain discretionary powers, especially in special circumstances like hung assemblies or constitutional crises. 
• The Governor plays a key role in legislative processes, such as giving assent to bills, summoning or dissolving the state legislature, and recommending President's rule under **Article 356** of the Constitution. 
• **Sikkim:** 
• Sikkim became the **22nd state of India** in **1975** through a constitutional amendment. It has a population of approximately **6.7 lakh** (as per Census 2011). 
• The state's economy is primarily based on **agriculture, tourism, and hydroelectric power**. It is also known for its organic farming practices. 
• Geographically, it is located in the **Himalayan range**, making it ecologically and strategically significant. 
• **Om Prakash Mathur:** 
• Om Prakash Mathur is a senior BJP leader from **Rajasthan**. He has previously served as a Member of Parliament in the **Rajya Sabha**. 
• He is known for his expertise in organizational management and political strategy, contributing to the expansion of the BJP in various regions. 
• His deep understanding of governance and public policy makes him a suitable choice for the role of Governor. 
• **Appointment of Governors:** 
• The Governor of a state is appointed by the **President of India** for a term of **five years**, but they can continue in office at the pleasure of the President. 
• The Governor's appointment often reflects a balance of administrative expertise, political considerations, and regional representation. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:** 
• **Article 153:** Provides for a Governor in each state. 
• **Article 155:** The Governor is appointed by the President of India. 
• **Article 156:** Specifies the term of office and conditions for removal of a Governor. 
• **Governors in Northeastern States:** 
• The role of Governors in states like Sikkim is crucial due to their **geopolitical significance** and proximity to international borders. 
• Governors often act as a bridge between the central government and the state government in these regions. </ul

questions.question:
In June 2025, EPFO's revised his auto-settlement limit. This limit is now

Rs. ____ lakh.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 5 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **EPFO (Employees' Provident Fund Organisation)** revised its auto-settlement limit in **June 2025** to **Rs. 5 lakh**, enhancing the scope of automated claim settlement processes for its members.
 
• The **auto-settlement mechanism** is a system introduced to provide faster and more efficient claim processing, ensuring timely disbursal of funds to beneficiaries without manual intervention.
 
• This decision aligns with the **EPFO’s goal** of leveraging technology to simplify the claims process and reduce delays for its members.
 
• The limit was raised from previous thresholds to **Rs. 5 lakh**, ensuring a larger number of claims are covered under the automatic system, benefiting employees and retirees.
 
• The enhancement of this limit is expected to significantly improve the **service delivery efficiency**, reduce the workload of the EPFO staff, and improve customer satisfaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **EPFO Overview:**

 
 
• The **Employees' Provident Fund Organisation** is a statutory body under the **Ministry of Labour and Employment**, Government of India, established in **1952**.
 
• EPFO manages the provident fund (PF), pension, and insurance schemes for employees in India.
 
• It ensures social security for employees by providing retirement benefits and financial aid during unemployment or emergencies.
 
 
 
• **What is Auto-Settlement?**
 
 
• The **auto-settlement process** in EPFO refers to the automated processing of claims, where eligible claims are settled without manual intervention.
 
• This mechanism is designed to minimize errors, reduce processing time, and provide better services to EPFO members.
 
• Claims such as **partial withdrawals**, pension benefits, and final settlement are processed through this system.
 
• With the revised limit of **Rs. 5 lakh**, more claims will be processed automatically, offering faster access to funds for employees.
 
 
 
• **Importance of EPFO’s Auto-Settlement Process:**
 
 
• It minimizes manual errors, ensuring accurate and timely disbursal of funds.
 
• Automated claims reduce the workload on EPFO staff, allowing them to focus on more complex issues and cases.
 
• It enhances the transparency and efficiency of the overall claims process.
 
• Beneficiaries can access their entitled funds quickly, especially during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Other Measures by EPFO:**
 
 
• EPFO has been actively working on digitizing its services, offering facilities like **online claim submissions**, **e-nomination**, and **UMANG App** for members to access services seamlessly.
 
• It also provides services like **passbook access**, **UAN activation**, and grievance redressal through online platforms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for EPFO Membership:**

 
 
• All organizations with **20 or more employees** are required to register with EPFO.
 
• Employees drawing a monthly salary of **up to Rs. 15,000** are eligible for mandatory EPF contributions.
 
 
 
• **EPFO Schemes:**
 
 
• **Employees' Provident Fund Scheme (EPFS), 1952:** Provides retirement benefits to employees.
 
• **Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI), 1976:** Provides life insurance benefits to employees.
 
• **Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS), 1995:** Provides pension to employees after retirement.
 
 
 
• **EPFO Initiatives:**
 
 
• Introduction of **UMANG App** for accessing EPFO services online.
 
• Implementation of a **Universal Account Number (UAN)** for portability and ease of access.
 
• Digitalization of services to enhance **transparency** and **efficiency**.
 
• Regularly increasing the auto-settlement limits to improve service delivery and reduce delays.

questions.question: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has on 4 August 2025 issued a detailed response to certain concerns raised on the impact of ____ percent Ethanol Blended Petrol on mileage and vehicle life.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 percent**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas** issued a response on **4 August 2025** addressing concerns regarding the impact of **20 percent Ethanol Blended Petrol (E20)** on mileage and vehicle life. 
• E20 is a fuel blend containing **20% ethanol and 80% petrol**. It is part of India's strategy to promote the use of renewable energy and reduce dependence on fossil fuels. 
• The introduction of E20 aligns with the **National Bio-Energy Policy** and India's commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions as part of the **Paris Agreement**. 
• Studies and trials conducted by the government and research institutions show that vehicles manufactured after **2023** are compatible with E20 fuel. However, older vehicles may require modifications to avoid potential damage to their engines. 
• Higher ethanol blends like E20 have been shown to slightly reduce mileage in conventional engines but can improve **octane levels**, leading to smoother combustion and reduced emissions. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Ethanol Blending Program (EBP):** 
• Launched in **2003**, the Ethanol Blending Program is aimed at blending ethanol with petrol to reduce dependency on crude oil imports and lower carbon emissions. 
• The Government of India announced the target of achieving a **20% ethanol blend** (E20) by **2025**, advancing the previous target of **2030**. 
• Ethanol is primarily derived from **sugarcane, maize, and surplus food grains**, providing an additional revenue stream for farmers. 
• **Benefits of Ethanol Blended Petrol:** 
• Helps in **reducing vehicular emissions** such as carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, and particulate matter. 
• Improves **fuel security** by reducing the import of crude oil, saving valuable foreign exchange. 
• Promotes the use of renewable energy resources and supports the agricultural sector. 
• **Challenges of Ethanol Blending:** 
• High ethanol content can lead to **corrosion** of engine parts if vehicles are not designed for such blends. 
• Blending requires significant investment in infrastructure, including dedicated storage facilities, blending units, and distribution networks. 
• Availability of adequate **feedstock** (like sugarcane and maize) is essential for large-scale ethanol production. 
• **Global Context:** 
• Countries like **Brazil** and the **United States** have successfully adopted ethanol blending programs. For example, Brazil uses ethanol blends up to **27%** in its fuel. 
• India's shift towards E20 is inspired by global best practices and aims to promote energy sustainability. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Impact on Engine:** Vehicles not designed for E20 might experience reduced mileage and potential damage to fuel systems. Proper adaptation of engines is essential for compatibility. 
• **Government Initiatives:** Subsidies and incentives for ethanol production and blending facilities are being provided to boost the adoption of E20. 
• **Economic Benefits:** E20 can significantly reduce India’s crude oil import bill and provide a sustainable market for agricultural produce.

questions.question: ____ was the first Indian to win a medal in Birmingham Commonwealth Games
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanket Sargar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Sanket Sargar** became the first Indian to win a medal at the **2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games**.

• He achieved this milestone in the **Men's 55 kg weightlifting category**, where he secured the **silver medal**.

• Sargar lifted a total of **248 kg** (113 kg in snatch and 135 kg in clean and jerk).

questions.question: The Aravalli Green Wall Project is a major initiative to spread green cover in the ____ km buffer area around the Aravalli hill range.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**60 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aravalli Green Wall Project** is a significant initiative by the Indian government to enhance environmental sustainability and combat desertification in the region surrounding the **Aravalli hill range**.
 
• The project aims to spread a green cover in a buffer area of **60 km** around the Aravalli hills, addressing ecological concerns such as deforestation, soil erosion, and climatic changes in the region.
 
• It seeks to create a natural barrier against the expansion of the **Thar Desert** into adjoining areas, thereby protecting biodiversity and promoting sustainable development.
 
• The initiative includes measures such as **afforestation, reforestation, and community engagement** to ensure effective implementation and long-term environmental benefits.
 
• The project is part of India's broader commitment to achieving the goals of the **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)**, which aims to restore degraded land and combat climate change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aravalli Hill Range:**

 
 
• The **Aravalli Hills** are one of the oldest mountain ranges in India, stretching across the states of **Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat, and Delhi**.
 
• They play a vital role in maintaining ecological balance by providing habitat for diverse flora and fauna and acting as a green barrier against desertification.
 
• Over the years, the Aravalli range has been adversely affected by **deforestation, illegal mining, and urbanization**, leading to environmental degradation.
 
 
 
• **Desertification:**
 
 
• **Desertification** refers to the process by which fertile land becomes desert, typically due to drought, deforestation, or inappropriate agricultural practices.
 
• The Aravalli Green Wall Project aims to mitigate desertification by increasing vegetation cover and enhancing soil quality in the region surrounding the Aravalli hills.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD):**
 
 
• The **UNCCD** is an international treaty aimed at combating desertification and promoting sustainable land management.
 
• India is a signatory to the UNCCD and has undertaken various initiatives, including the Aravalli Green Wall Project, to fulfill its commitments under this treaty.
 
 
 
• **Afforestation and Reforestation:**
 
 
• **Afforestation** refers to the process of creating forests in areas that were not previously forested, while **reforestation** involves replanting trees in deforested areas.
 
• Both strategies are integral to the Aravalli Green Wall Project and are aimed at restoring ecological balance and improving air quality in the region.
 
 
 
• **Community Participation:**
 
 
• The project emphasizes the role of local communities in its implementation, encouraging participation in tree plantation drives and sustainable land management practices.
 
• This ensures long-term sustainability and promotes environmental awareness among residents.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Thar Desert Expansion:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert, located primarily in Rajasthan, is expanding due to climate change and human activities such as deforestation and overgrazing.
 
• The Aravalli Green Wall Project aims to act as a natural shield to prevent further desert expansion into fertile regions.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Challenges:**
 
 
• Deforestation and illegal mining in the Aravalli region have led to significant environmental challenges, including soil erosion, loss of biodiversity, and reduced groundwater levels.
 
• The project seeks to address these issues by restoring ecological balance and promoting sustainable practices.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Aravalli Green Wall Project is part of broader government efforts to combat climate change and promote sustainable development.
 
• Other initiatives include **National Afforestation Programme** and **Green India Mission**, which aim to increase forest cover and improve ecosystem services.
 
 
 
• **Role of Local Authorities:**
 
 
• State governments and local authorities play a crucial role in implementing the project, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations and engaging communities.
 
• Collaboration between central and state governments is essential for the project's success.

questions.question: Which festival of Kerala has entered the Guinness World Records for being the single largest gathering of women for a religious activity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Attukal Pongala**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• **Attukal Pongala** is a famous festival celebrated in the state of **Kerala**, India. It is organized annually at the **Attukal Bhagavathy Temple** in Thiruvananthapuram. 
• The festival is renowned for its unique feature of being the **largest single gathering of women** in the world for a religious activity. This achievement has been recognized by the **Guinness World Records**. 
• The event involves thousands of women preparing a special offering called **Pongala**, made of rice, jaggery, and coconut, which is cooked in earthen pots as an offering to the goddess Attukal Devi. 
• The festival spans over ten days, with the **Pongala ritual** being the most significant and occurring on the ninth day. Women gather in and around the temple premises and on the streets of Thiruvananthapuram to participate in this ritual. 
• The festival is a symbolic representation of **devotion, equality, and empowerment of women**, as it unites women from all walks of life and religious backgrounds. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Significance of Attukal Pongala:** 
• The festival is dedicated to **Attukal Bhagavathy**, an incarnation of the Hindu goddess **Kannaki (Parvati).** 
• It is celebrated in the **Malayalam month of Kumbham** (February–March). 
• The festival represents the victory of good over evil and celebrates the **goddess’s power** to protect her devotees. 
• **Guinness World Records Recognition:** 
• The **2016 edition** of Attukal Pongala saw participation from more than **2.5 million women**, earning it the Guinness World Record for the **largest gathering of women** for a religious activity. 
• The record highlights the global cultural significance of the festival and its ability to bring women together in solidarity. 
• **Preparation for the Ritual:** 
• Women bring their own cooking utensils, ingredients, and firewood to prepare the Pongala offering on temporary hearths set up on roadsides and open spaces. 
• The ritual begins after the chief priest of the temple lights the **holy hearth (Pandara Aduppu)** inside the temple premises. 
• **Comparison with Other Kerala Festivals:** 
• **Chikalkalo:** A traditional mud festival celebrated in certain parts of Kerala, particularly in the Kasaragod district. It involves physical games and is not religious in nature. 
• **Pooram:** A temple festival celebrated with grand processions and fireworks. The most famous is the Thrissur Pooram. 
• **Vishu:** The Malayalam New Year celebrated in April, marked by feasting and the Vishukkani ritual. 
• **Attukal Pongala:** Stands out as a festival exclusively for women and holds spiritual and cultural importance. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Historical Background:** The temple is believed to be over **500 years old** and holds a significant place in Kerala's religious and cultural history. 
• **Equality and Inclusiveness:** Women from all castes, religions, and social backgrounds participate in the festival, making it a symbol of **unity and empowerment.** 
• **Economic Impact:** The festival contributes significantly to the local economy, as vendors sell cooking materials, food items, and earthen pots during the event.

questions.question: Around which year was Robert Clive appointed the Governor of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1764**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Robert Clive** was appointed the **Governor of Bengal** in **1764** after his significant military and administrative contributions during his tenure in India. 
• Clive played a major role in the **Battle of Plassey (1757)**, which marked the beginning of British dominance in India. 
• As Governor, Clive implemented **dual government** in Bengal, combining British administrative control with local Nawab rule. 
• He was instrumental in establishing the **foundation of British rule** in India by securing significant economic and political advantages for the British East India Company. 
• His tenure faced criticism due to alleged corruption and exploitation, but his policies laid the groundwork for British colonial administration in India. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Robert Clive:** 
• Born in **1725**, Clive is often regarded as the architect of British supremacy in India. 
• He first arrived in India as a clerk for the **East India Company** and later rose to prominence due to his military success. 
• **Battle of Plassey (1757):** 
• The battle was fought between the British East India Company, under Clive, and **Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah**, the ruler of Bengal. 
• Clive's tactical brilliance and treachery within the Nawab's camp led to British victory. 
• This victory allowed the British East India Company to gain control over Bengal's **wealth and resources**. 
• **Dual Government System:** 
• Introduced by Clive in Bengal after 1765, it divided administrative responsibilities between the British and the local Nawabs. 
• While the British controlled revenue collection and military power, the Nawabs were nominally responsible for law and order. 
• This system allowed the East India Company to exploit Bengal's wealth without direct administrative costs. 
• **Controversies Surrounding Clive:** 
• Clive faced allegations of corruption and profiteering during his tenure. 
• In **1772**, he was subject to an inquiry by the British Parliament but was ultimately acquitted. 
• Despite controversies, his contributions to British imperial expansion in India remain significant. 
• **Legacy:** 
• Clive's policies laid the foundation for British colonial administration and economic exploitation in India. 
• He died in **1774**, leaving behind a mixed legacy as a military strategist and controversial administrator. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **1765 Treaty of Allahabad:** 
• Signed between Clive and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II. 
• Granted the British East India Company **Diwani rights** (revenue collection) in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa. 
• **Economic Impact of Clive's Policies:** 
• Led to the exploitation of Bengal's resources, contributing to the **Great Bengal Famine (1770)**. 
• Clive's revenue policies prioritized British profits over local welfare. 
• **Military Achievements:** 
• Clive's victories in India established British dominance over French and local rulers. 
• Played a crucial role in defeating the French during the **Carnatic Wars**. </ul

questions.question: In which year did the committee for reforms in the insurance sector formed under the chairmanship of R.N. Malhotra submitted its report?

__

• The **Malhotra Committee** was formed in **1993** by the Government of India to suggest reforms in the **insurance sector**.

• The committee was chaired by **R.N. Malhotra**, the former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

• It submitted its report in the year **1994**, recommending several pivotal changes to liberalize and modernize the Indian insurance sector.

• The report emphasized the need for opening up the insurance sector to **private players** and the establishment of an independent **regulatory authority** to oversee insurance activities.

• The recommendations of the Malhotra Committee laid the groundwork for the formation of the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** in 1999.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Key Recommendations of the Malhotra Committee:**

• Opening up the Indian insurance market to **private sector** participation to foster competition and efficiency.

• Introducing **foreign direct investment (FDI)** in the insurance sector, with a cap of 26% initially, which was later increased to 49% and subsequently to 74% in 2021.

• Establishing an independent regulatory body, which resulted in the creation of the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** in 1999.

• Allowing private companies to enter both **life insurance** and **non-life insurance** sectors.

• Restructuring the public sector insurance companies to operate on a more competitive basis.

• **Impact of the Malhotra Committee Report:**

• The recommendations led to the liberalization of the Indian insurance market in the **early 2000s**.

• Private sector players like **HDFC Life, ICICI Lombard, Max Life**, and others entered the market, increasing competition and improving service quality.

• The establishment of IRDAI brought about **transparency** and **uniform regulations** for the insurance sector.

• Insurance penetration in India improved significantly, with more people opting for life and non-life insurance policies.

• **About R.N. Malhotra:**

• **R.N. Malhotra** served as the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) from **1985 to 1990**.

• He was instrumental in shaping financial reforms in India and played a key role in the liberalization process of the insurance sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI):**

• Established in **1999** as an independent regulatory body to oversee insurance activities in India.

• Its objectives include protecting the interests of policyholders, promoting healthy competition, and ensuring the financial stability of the insurance market.

• **Liberalization of the Insurance Sector:**

• The entry of private players and FDI brought technological advancements and customer-centric services to the industry.

• Insurance penetration increased from **2.15% (2001)** to **4.2% (2021)**, as per IRDAI reports.

questions.question: What subject does Article 77 of the Indian Constitution pertain to?

options.text: Conduct of business of the Government of India
Council of Ministers to aid and advise President

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Conduct of business of the Government of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 77 of the Indian Constitution** pertains to the **conduct of business of the Government of India**. It outlines how the executive actions and decisions of the Government are to be carried out.
 
• It states that all executive actions of the Government of India should be expressed in the name of the **President of India**.
 
• It also specifies the rules for the allocation of business among the different **Ministries and Departments** of the Government.
 
• The President is empowered to make rules for the more convenient transaction of business and for its distribution among the Ministers.
 
• This Article ensures that the functioning of the Government is streamlined, organized, and accountable under the framework of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **President's Role in Executive Actions:**

 
 
• All executive actions of the Government of India are performed in the name of the **President**, as per Article 77.
 
• The **President** acts on the advice of the **Council of Ministers**, headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• This ensures that the executive authority is exercised within the framework of parliamentary democracy.
 
 
 
• **Rules for Allocation of Business:**
 
 
• The President has the authority to frame rules for the allocation of business among the **Ministers**.
 
• These rules are crucial for ensuring the **smooth functioning** of the Government and avoiding overlapping responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **Accountability in Governance:**
 
 
• Article 77 mandates that all executive actions be conducted transparently, ensuring **accountability** to the Parliament and the citizens.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a clear and organized system for executing the policies and decisions of the Government.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Article 74:**
 
 
• While Article 77 deals with the conduct of business, **Article 74** deals with the Council of Ministers aiding and advising the President.
 
• Both Articles collectively ensure the smooth operation of the **executive branch** of the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• All official communications, like **notifications and orders**, are issued in the name of the President.
 
• For instance, appointment letters for high-ranking officials like Governors and Supreme Court judges bear the President’s name.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 77 and Parliamentary Democracy:**

 
 
• Article 77 is integral to India's system of **parliamentary democracy**, where the executive is accountable to the legislature.
 
• It ensures a uniform system for the **execution of policies and legal frameworks** as determined by the Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework for Ministries:**
 
 
• This Article provides a legal basis for the formation and functioning of various **Ministries** and **Departments** within the Government.
 
• It enables Ministers to act within their allocated portfolios and ensures **clarity in decision-making**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Article 77 was drafted as part of the Constitution of India, which came into effect on **26 January 1950**.
 
• The Article was inspired by the British system of governance and adapted to fit India’s parliamentary model.

questions.question: Members of the Legislative Council of an Indian state as nearly as may be, ____ shall be elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards and such other local authorities in the State as Parliament may by law specify.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1/3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 171** of the Constitution of India specifies the composition of the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) for states that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• As per **Article 171(3)(a)**, **1/3 of the members** of the Legislative Council are elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards, and other local authorities in the state.
 
• The provision ensures representation from local self-governing bodies, which play a vital role in state governance.
 
• These members are chosen through an electoral process where representatives from various local bodies vote to elect Legislative Council members.
 
• This mechanism provides a democratic way to include local governance in the legislative process, fostering decentralized decision-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Legislative Council:**

 
 
• The Legislative Council is the upper house of the state legislature in states with bicameral legislatures (e.g., Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka).
 
• Its members are elected, nominated, or indirectly appointed through various processes outlined in Article 171.
 
• The Council must not exceed **one-third** of the total membership of the Legislative Assembly of the state.
 
 
 
• **Election Process:**
 
 
• Members elected by local authorities constitute **1/3** of the total members of the Legislative Council.
 
• Other members are elected by graduates, teachers, members of the Legislative Assembly, or nominated by the Governor.
 
• The election process is conducted by the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
 
 
• **Role of Local Authorities:**
 
 
• Local authorities such as municipalities and district boards play a significant role in state governance.
 
• Representation from local bodies ensures that issues relevant to local administration are addressed in the state legislature.
 
• This system strengthens participatory democracy by incorporating grassroots-level governance into the legislative framework.
 
 
 
• **States with Legislative Councils:**
 
 
• Currently, only **6 states** in India have Legislative Councils: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.
 
• States can propose the creation or abolition of Legislative Councils, but the final decision rests with Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The bicameral system in state legislatures was established to include diverse perspectives in law-making.
 
• The inclusion of local authorities in the election process reflects the significance of grassroots governance in India.
 
• It was introduced to balance representation from different sections of society and administrative units.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 171:** Defines the composition and electoral process for Legislative Councils in states with bicameral legislatures.
 
• **Representation:** Ensures inclusion of local self-governance bodies in the legislative process through elections.
 
• **Governor’s Role:** The Governor nominates 1/6th of the members of the Legislative Council, typically experts in various fields like literature, science, or social service.
 
• **Election Eligibility:** Members of municipalities, district boards, and other local authorities are eligible to vote in the elections for Legislative Council members.
 
• **Relevance:** Legislative Councils provide an additional layer of checks and balances in state governance, complementing the Legislative Assembly.
